name: PureDash Cleaner
author: rahajason

sections.description:
PureDash Cleaner helps you clean up your WordPress dashboard without writing CSS or editing theme files. Turn on Zen Mode, click the element you no longer want to see, confirm, and it stays hidden on every admin page. Every hidden element is listed on a settings page, so you can bring it back at any time.

It is useful when plugin banners pile up, when the Dashboard screen is full of widgets nobody reads, or when you want a simpler admin area for the people who log in to a site you manage.

What you can hide

  • Admin notices – hide admin notices such as promotional banners, review requests and other messages you have already read.
  • Dashboard widgets – remove dashboard widgets like Activity, Quick Draft, WordPress Events and News, or boxes added by other plugins.
  • Admin menu items – hide top-level admin menu entries or individual submenu links you never use.
  • Admin bar items – hide individual links in the toolbar at the top of admin pages.
  • Other page elements – almost any other visible block inside wp-admin can be selected.

Some core areas are protected and cannot be selected, such as the whole admin bar, the whole admin menu, the main content area and PureDash Cleaner’s own controls. This keeps you from locking yourself out of the interface.

How Zen Mode works

Zen Mode is the selection tool. Start it from the PureDash Cleaner menu in the admin bar. While it is on, a blue outline follows your mouse and clicking an element selects it instead of following links. A dialog then shows the detected element type and lets you add a label to recognize it later. Press Esc to leave Zen Mode without hiding anything.

You can also tick Hide temporarily (Reload to reset). The element disappears from the current page only, nothing is saved, and it comes back as soon as you reload.

Managing and restoring hidden elements

Go to Settings > PureDash Cleaner to see every saved rule, grouped by category: Main Menu, Admin Bar, Dashboard Widgets, Admin Notices and Miscellaneous. From there you can rename a rule or delete it to make the element visible again. A Reset All Settings option removes every rule at once, and Safe Mode lets you switch off all rules for your own account if you hid something by mistake.

Who sees the changes

Only users who can manage site options (administrators by default) can use Zen Mode and manage rules. Rules are stored once for the whole site and apply to every logged-in user who has a role on it, whatever that role is. They are not limited to the account that created them.

Good to know

  • Hiding is visual only. Elements are hidden with CSS. Nothing is deleted, the plugin or feature behind an element keeps running, and hiding a menu link does not block access to its page. Do not rely on this plugin to restrict what users can do; use roles and capabilities for that.
  • Rules apply inside wp-admin only. The admin bar shown on the front end of your site is not changed.
  • No per-role choice in this version. Every rule applies to all user roles that exist on the site when the rule is saved. A role created later is not covered by existing rules.
  • Rules depend on page markup. If another plugin changes the HTML of a notice or widget, for example after an update, a rule may stop matching and the element can reappear. Hide it again with Zen Mode.
  • One rule can match several elements. If the selected element shares its selector with others, the dialog warns you before you confirm.

Privacy Policy

This plugin utilizes the Freemius SDK to provide optional usage tracking and support services. Data is only sent to freemius.com if you explicitly opt in during activation. For more information, please refer to the Freemius Privacy Policy: https://freemius.com/privacy/

How to Use

Hiding an element with Zen Mode

  1. Log in to your WordPress admin as an administrator.
  2. Look for the PureDash Cleaner entry in the top admin bar (black bar at the top). Hover over it to open the submenu.
  3. Click Toggle Zen Mode. The page enters selection mode and a blue highlight follows your cursor as you move over admin elements.
  4. Hover over the element you want to hide (a menu item, a dashboard widget, an admin notice, etc.) and click it.
  5. A dialog appears. Optionally give the element a label so you can identify it later, then click Hide Element to confirm.
  6. The rule is saved and the page reloads. The element is now hidden on every admin page for all logged-in users of the site, not only for you, until you delete the rule.

If you tick Hide temporarily (Reload to reset) in step 5, nothing is saved: the element is only hidden on the current page until you reload it.

Viewing and managing hidden elements

  1. Go to Settings > PureDash Cleaner.
  2. The Blocked Elements tab lists every element that has been hidden on the site, grouped by category (Main Menu, Admin Bar, Dashboard Widgets, Admin Notices, Miscellaneous).
  3. To restore an element, click the Delete button next to it. It reappears on the next page load.
  4. To rename a rule’s label, click the pencil icon next to its name.
  5. To remove every rule at once, use Reset All Settings in the Help & Safe Mode tab or in the admin bar menu. This cannot be undone.

Safe Mode (emergency recovery)

If you accidentally hide something you need and cannot navigate:

  • Add ?puredash_safe_mode=1 to any admin URL, for example: https://yoursite.com/wp-admin/?puredash_safe_mode=1. Rules are disabled for that page load only.
  • Or go to Settings > PureDash Cleaner > Help & Safe Mode and click Activate Safe Mode. Rules stay disabled for your user account until you click Exit Safe Mode (in the notice at the top of the page or in the admin bar menu).

Safe Mode only affects your own view. Other users keep seeing the site with all rules applied. Use it to reach the settings page and delete the problematic rule.

Developer options

To disable the plugin entirely without deactivating it, add this line to your wp-config.php:

define( 'PUREDASH_DISABLE', true );

To stop rules from being added, deleted or renamed from Zen Mode and the settings page, add the following line (the Reset All Settings option is not affected):

define( 'PUREDASH_LOCK_SETTINGS', true );
sections.installation:
1. Upload the puredash-cleaner folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory, or install the plugin from Plugins > Add New by searching for “PureDash Cleaner”.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ menu in WordPress.
  3. Go to Settings > PureDash Cleaner to access the plugin settings page.
sections.faq:
Where is the settings page?

Go to Settings > PureDash Cleaner in the WordPress admin menu, or click PureDash Cleaner in the top admin bar and choose Settings.

I accidentally hid something important. How do I get it back?

Add ?puredash_safe_mode=1 to your admin URL (e.g. https://yoursite.com/wp-admin/?puredash_safe_mode=1). This disables all rules for that page load so you can open Settings > PureDash Cleaner and delete the rule. The whole admin menu and admin bar are protected and cannot be hidden, but individual entries inside them can.

Does this hide elements for all users or just me?

For all users. Rules are saved for the whole site and apply to every logged-in user with a role on it, including editors, authors and other non-admin roles. Only administrators (users who can manage options) can create, rename or delete rules. To check the screen without your rules, use Safe Mode: it only affects your own account.

Does hiding a menu item stop users from opening that page?

No. PureDash Cleaner hides elements visually. The page behind a hidden menu link is still reachable by anyone who has permission to open it, for example by typing its URL.

Does it delete notices, widgets or plugin data?

No. Hidden elements are still generated by WordPress and by your plugins; they are simply not displayed. Delete the rule and the element comes back.

Does it change the front end of my site?

No. Rules are applied on admin pages only.
sections.changelog:
1.2.14

  • Fixed the “Upgrade to Pro” button in the Hide Element dialog, which linked to a broken wp-admin/undefined URL.
  • Rewrote the plugin description and readme: clearer feature list, who the hidden elements apply to, and known limits.

1.2.13

  • Internal build cleanup: removed leftover CI/build script files from the distributed plugin package.

1.2.12

  • Fixed a build script bug that had been silently removing the free “Edit Label” action from the Blocked Elements list.

1.2.11

  • Fixed clean-premium.py stripping the ‘is_premium’ Freemius flag entirely on WordPress.org builds instead of setting it to false; the SDK defaults it to true when absent, which made the free build behave as if it were the premium package.

1.2.10

  • Security/Plugin Check: replaced phpcs:ignore suppressions (not honored by the official Plugin Check tool for security sniffs) with real fixes — proper nonce verification tied to the Safe Mode toggle’s $_GET read, nested $_FILES key validation for the config import, and sanitize-at-read for the white-label applied-roles field.

1.2.9

  • Fixed remaining WordPress Plugin Check findings: outdated “Tested up to” header (readme.txt and the plugin file docblock), and missing wp_unslash() on white-label color fields.

1.2.8

  • Replaced the textual promo banner with an image banner in the “Hide Element” modal for a cleaner look.

1.2.7

  • Fixed admin bar “PureDash Cleaner” link pointing to a non-existent page (admin.php) instead of the correct settings page (Settings > PureDash Cleaner).
  • Expanded readme with a full “How to Use” section, FAQ, and Safe Mode recovery instructions to help users configure and use the plugin from scratch.

1.2.6

  • Security: Added CSS-context sanitization for selector values output via wp_add_inline_style() to prevent potential CSS injection.
  • Updated Freemius SDK to 2.13.2.
  • Added plugin owner to the Contributors list in readme.txt.

1.2.5

  • WordPress.org release: removed premium-only code and upgrade links.
  • Fixed the “Edit Label” action on the Blocked Elements list.
  • Simplified the Hide Element dialog.

1.0.3

  • Updated version to 1.0.3.

1.0.2

  • Renamed plugin to PureDash Cleaner for WordPress.org compliance.
  • Ensured compatibility with official directory requirements.
  • Integrated Freemius SDK with Org-compliant configuration.
  • Removed inline styles and scripts for better security.

short_description: Point, click, hide: remove the admin notices, dashboard widgets, menu items and toolbar links that clutter your WordPress dashboard. No code needed.
